decision_rule: Across every checkpoint at or after the formed checkpoint, the pooled quality's range, its largest value minus its smallest, must stay within 0.10. A wider range means the counter keeps moving, which feeds a drift reading when the movement runs one way in training steps and an unclassifiable reading when it does not. A checkpoint with no measurable quality would leave the range unavailable, recorded as RANGE_NOT_COMPUTABLE, which cannot arise while every checkpoint reports a number.
metric: Range of the held-out pooled quality across every checkpoint at or after the formed checkpoint.
notes: Two crossings are computed, both measured up from the baseline floor toward the committed anchor quality. The pooled quality first reaching the half-distance point locates when the counter becomes usable; that crossing decides whether formation counts as early or late against step16000. The pooled quality first reaching the nine-tenths point marks where the stability test starts, for both channels. The committed gate record assigns each crossing that job in its second and fourth answers of record. The design object's third endpoint states the early-late comparison against the nine-tenths crossing instead, so both comparisons are recorded and the reading follows the committed answer. If either integrity gate recorded in these values failed, this record is void as evidence about the model, and is an instrument fault only. A further run of this script on the same box is a rerun of the same instrument, not a replication.
